decisions.reason: A standard catalogue variant within the firm's core display range, presented publicly on its own page, costs little to keep and fits the announced display focus, so management has no reason to write it off.
The pegboard-back shelf display was visibly committed to on its own page and belongs to the firm's core competence, so dropping it would mean admitting a misjudgement for little gain.
The quarter-pallet shelf display is a staple format of the firm's one-stop display offer, and its continued public presentation supports persistence.
The eighth-pallet display complements the established pallet sizes and uses existing design and production capacity, so it is worth keeping as part of the announced range.

The wooden pallet display required more distinct investment outside the cardboard core, and that sunk commitment, together with the possibility of blaming weak results on temporary pandemic-era retail disruption, favours keeping it despite slightly higher drop risk.
The media-products display faces structural decline in physical media demand, but it is low-cost to keep within the core range and was publicly presented, so management is likely to persist for now.
